# dsh-context-decay
简体中文
Model-driven, **lossy** context decay for DeepSeek Harness.

The model decides when and what to compress. Finished spans are replaced by
self-written summaries;

the current turn is always kept. There is no recovery:
the summary is the only surviving record.

> **Install note:** This is a **manual-install** plugin: it requires a DSH
> checkout with the `mode

lMessageDecoration` seam and is not a drop-in
> plugin-market bundle (see Requirements).
## What it does

- **Inline position anchors.** Every model-addressable message with a visible
text block is prefixed

with `⟦p<number>⟧`; tool-call-only assistant turns are
unanchored by design. Compression ranges use

those anchors directly:
`⟦p<from>⟧ summary ⟦p<to>⟧`. Anchors are presentation, never part of the co

ntent.
- **Copied anchors removed.** If the model starts a reply with one or more
anchors, the leadi

ng run is stripped at the request boundary and again before
the reply is committed, so the transcrip

t and later requests stay clean.
- **Model-selected spans.** The model calls `compress` with one or

more
half-open ranges and writes each summary itself. No extra summarizer request.
Split around cont

ent that must stay live; pass all consumed spans in one call
so the prefix is not invalidated repeat

edly.
- **Lossy by design.** Compressed content is gone. There is no `decompress`, no
original-text

search, and no external table. The summary must be self-contained.
- **Tool results are compressible

.** All results of one assistant tool-call
message must stay in the same span. A boundary inside tha

ive turn and its tool results cannot be
compressed. If the turn starts with unanchored system/runtim

e messages, a `to`
boundary at its first visible anchor keeps those messages and compresses only
the

history before the turn; `"end"` remains the end-of-compressible-history
sentinel.
- **Tiered re-co

mpression.** Compressing a live summary block again produces a
tier-2 summary; larger merges increas

e the tier. `drop` removes a block
completely with no tombstone.
- **Pressure without automation.**

The plugin reports context pressure and
injects a reminder on each growth step; the reminder level f

ollows the current
pressure band, and the critical band uses a shorter step. It never compresses
aut

omatically; the model decides.
- **Live panel + audit.** A sidebar panel shows pressure, blocks, pos

itions,
request counts, and the reminder ledger. An optional JSONL audit records each
request and co

quest counts, and the reminder ledger. An optional JSONL audit records each
request and compression.
## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness **0.2.1-rc.2** with the local host patch in
`patches/dsh-model-message-decoration

.patch`
applied. Stock DSH does not expose the decoration seam; there is no runtime
fallback. Instal

lation alone is not enough: rebuild the host after patching.
- Node.js **>= 22.19**.
- A web profile

. The client half needs the sidebar/session/locale UI packages
listed in `package.json`.
- The bundl

e patch disables official **automatic** compaction
(`compaction-basic.auto: false`), keeps the manua

l `/compact` command, and
disables the in-place surface rewriters (`tool-result-pruner`,
`image-offl

oad`) when those rows exist. `/compact` remains an emergency
host fallback; its checkpoint is not a
context-decay block.

## Tools
| Tool | Purpose |
| `compress({spans:[{from,to,summary,topic?}]})` | Replace one or more half-open ranges with self-wr
itten summaries. `from`/`to` are visible anchor texts such as `"⟦p12⟧"` (bare `"p12"` and integer `1
2` also work); `to` may also be `"end"`. Several non-overlapping spans per call are allowed. Tool-gr

oup edges are rejected. |
| `drop({from,to})` | Remove exactly one live summary block. Use the block
's printed anchor pair; `"end"` is allowed for a tail block. No tombstone, no recovery. |

A live summary block prints its pair inline as `⟦p<from>⟧ summary ⟦p<to>⟧`; use that
[该节后续省略]
## How it works

The host patch adds a `modelMessageDecoration` service. The plugin registers a
decoration provider t

hat prefixes the messages selected by the replay state;
the agent loop, token meter, and request pay

load all apply the same decoration.
Positions come from the replayed surface, not from message text.

Compressions
append `compaction/start`, `compaction/summary`, a replacement user message, and
`comp
action/end`; replay rebuilds blocks, tiers, and the free list.

See `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` for the state model,
invariants, and failure modes.

See `docs/PROMPTS.zh-CN.md` for a Chinese translation of
the model-facing prompts, tool descriptions
, reminders, and error copy.
## Limitations and non-goals

- **No recovery.** There is no decompress, search, or spill archive. This is
deliberate; it is also

the main trade-off.
- **Requires a patched host.** The decoration seam is not upstream. Without it
t

he plugin cannot safely present anchors or replay positions.
- **No automatic compression.** Reminde

rs are advisory. A model may ignore them;
the budget stays protected by the request guard, not by si

lent compaction.
The official automatic policy is off; manual `/compact` remains available.
- **`/co

mpact` is a manual fallback.** It runs the official backend and writes an
official checkpoint, not a

context-decay tier block. Use it only when a
session is already too large for a normal request.
- *

*Manual install, not a market bundle.** A market index cannot express the
host-patch requirement, an

d `engines.dsh` cannot distinguish a patched host
from a stock one. Distribute the checkout or tarba

ll with the patch
instructions until the seam is upstream.
- **One compression backend per profile.*

* Do not run another compaction backend
or an in-place surface rewriter alongside it.
- **Replay dep

ends on the current event format.** Compression replay uses the
current `surfaceOp` and compaction e

current event format.** Compression replay uses the
current `surfaceOp` and compaction event shape.
